# Cyrus build: what exists and what needs the owner (updated 2026-10-10)

Nothing below is deployed, merged to main, migrated in production, or switched on. All work is on branches, verified on node-2 / devhost.

## Branches and worktrees (chain; later branches contain earlier ones)
- `feature/cyrus-r0` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r0): version registry, launch-pair guard, starter-grant guard, reproducible jars, engine core (spec, revisions, namespaces, router, asset gate), Test Flight, pack delivery (pack host, managed plugins, Pack Loader), 26.x lane (inert), eval set (124 prompts).
- `feature/cyrus-r1` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r1): texture slice, sound slice (+ library manifest/taxonomy/search), texture library + unified catalog layer.
- `feature/cyrus-r2` (/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-r2): r1 merged in + server inventory, conflict engine, Mod Packs. **The current integration branch.**
- `feature/cyrus-r3` (cyrus-r3): import-your-own-mod. DONE and merged into r2.
- `feature/cyrus-r4` (cyrus-r4): Data Pack Studio backend. DONE and merged into r2 (server.js/prompts.js conflicts resolved).
- `feature/cyrus-r5` (cyrus-r5): Studio UI part 1: shell, Texture Studio, locked states, library browser (in progress, from r2).
- `feature/cyrus-r6` (cyrus-r6): animated creature pipeline, BetterModel 3.5.0, 26.x first. DONE and merged into r2 (34 conflict blocks resolved; 1211 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r7` (cyrus-r7): gameplay designer engine (items + ability graph + 17-component library). DONE and merged into r2 (31 conflict blocks; 1325 Cyrus/builder tests pass; tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r8` (cyrus-r8): worldgen datapacks (custom dimensions/biomes/structures). DONE and merged into r2 (1394 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r9` (cyrus-r9): Sound Studio UI. DONE and merged into r2 (1468 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r10` (cyrus-r10): item model states + display contexts (bow pull, gun aim/reload, 8 contexts, studio In-game preview). DONE and merged into r2 (1429 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r11` (cyrus-r11): GUI menu + quest designers, extends the design kind. DONE and merged into r2 (1531 Cyrus/builder tests pass, tsc clean).
- `feature/cyrus-r12`: integration/delivery (release record, Test Flight gate, delivery orchestrator with proven rollback, sound relay, admin read model). DONE, merged into r2 together with r13-foundation (1596 tests pass).
- Studio UI part 1 (r5: shell, Texture Studio, library browser, locked states) is DONE and merged into r2.
- Queued next: Sound Studio UI, item model states and display contexts, animated creature pipeline (26.x), gameplay designers, then R4/R5 of the master plan.

## Switches (all OFF; fail closed)
`cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` (must move together; guard built), `cyrus_import_enabled`, `cyrus_studios_enabled`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1` (real plugin/pack install), `CYRUS_MODPACK_INSTALL_REAL=1`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1` (until set, customer builds get synth sounds only), `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` (render host), pack storage env (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE` + S3 settings).

## Needs your approval or action
1. **Production migrations** (additive, new tables only): `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-engine-core.sql` (4 tables + a trigger that must be run by hand), `2026-10-10-cyrus-managed-plugins.sql` (2 tables) then `scripts/cyrus-seed-managed-plugins.ts`. More may be added by in-progress agents (they report).
2. **VM 88001** (the deploy script /root/agent-notes/deploy-modbuilder.sh now copies every needed file incl. registry.json and deps.json; the Dockerfile COPY list was missing textures/sound modules before and is fixed and test-guarded): rebuild the build-service image with the new files (jar.js, textures.js, sound files, texture-example.json, datapack/import files when done), the JDK 25 build args, and make `registry.json` available inside the container; verify the hardened scan is live; check `/health` `auth` (API key vs subscription) and switch to an API key **before any public launch**; then one real build to confirm reproducible jars and the asset sections.
3. **Pack hosting**: choose storage provider/bucket (any S3 API; R2 has free egress), the public pack domain (`CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`), retention for unused packs; deploy the Pack Loader jar to the worker host.
4. **Sound library**: confirm Excelerator.tech is yours, document the source per file group, then set `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`; write the customer-facing sound licence; review `sound-library-catalog.md`; set the render path (ssh key to node-2, worker only).
5. **Reviews**: texture contact sheets (`texture-library-sheets/`), the studio design mockups (`/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/`), the 7 design defaults I chose (plan names Katara/Saka/Yakko, token cost shown on asset edits, packs optional with per-mod required option, 'Mob skin: coming soon', read-only mobile approve, full-page editors).
6. **Decisions**: should a Mod Pack with open warnings install without the user acknowledging them (today yes; I recommend requiring acknowledgement)? Import attestation wording and rate limits (when the import agent reports).
7. **Real-client test day** (someone with Minecraft): pack download and accept prompt, textures, item previews, sounds and subtitles, Bedrock note. Nothing resource-pack related is verified in a real client yet.
8. **Paid eval run**: approve a number of real builds and budget (the eval set is 124 prompts; a full multi-version run is 226 builds; ~30 texture prompts first); a baseline file is saved after the first run.
9. Delete when finished: `/tank/nxeon-build/tmp/r0-26x` (~2 GB) and old tmp dirs.

## Known limits (honest)
No real model build has been run for texture/sound/datapack/import sections, so the AI's output quality is unverified. No real client has loaded a pack. The vanilla-lookalike texture check is a stub. Test Flight runs one flight at a time with no container limits. 26.3 has no stable Paper build (only alpha/beta).

## Data pack studio decisions (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flags `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO` and `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL` are off. To go live: paid eval of model-written specs first, rebuild the service image (the Dockerfile list now includes the data pack modules), wire the delivery job (steps in docs). Decision: allow vanilla loot overrides? (out of v1). Known flaky test: test/cyrus-admin.test.ts fails only when run in the big parallel batch (passes alone, 31/31).

## Creature pipeline owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flags: `CYRUS_CREATURES=1`, `CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL=1`; mark a 26.x version buildable only after the image rebuild and an eval. Decide whether Nxeon pre-places BetterModel's libraries (it downloads 57 files on first start); place the BetterModel jar + seed the catalog; real-client test day (looks/animation unverified); the BetterModel pack hand-off must follow a server restart; suggested limit until a real-client test: 25 creatures per server, ~300 bones in one player's view. Template quality: ghoul and wolf good, the banshee reads correctly but its robe is blocky.

## Gameplay designer owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` is off. Decide: the pure 'just tweak a setting' parser `planDesignEdit` is exposed but NOT wired (skipping the model changes billing). Designer owns the main class/plugin.yml/config.yml; free-form Java only in `custom/`; every number/text/sound becomes an editable config setting; charged abilities = hold sneak then release. Not verified: any in-game behaviour (clicks, pulls, projectiles, recipes, loot), 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/26.1.2 javac (no classpath on node-2). Process note: each new asset kind touches the same 8 service/portal files, so agents must merge the latest feature/cyrus-r2 into their branch before finishing.

## Worldgen owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_WORLDGEN=1` (also needs `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`), off. IMPORTANT: a broken worldgen pack stops the whole server at its next start; the delivery job MUST roll back if the server does not come up after the restart, and that is NOT wired yet. Also decide: what happens to a dimension's world folder when its mod is uninstalled (currently kept); a small paid trial of model-written specs before enabling; image rebuild (Dockerfile updated). Limits: 2 dimensions, 16 biomes, 32+32 features, templates up to 48^3 / 32768 blocks, cost score cap 100. Performance: low cost runs on 2 GB+, medium needs 4 GB, high needs 8 GB plus pre-generation. Verified formats across 6 versions (1.21.2 carvers list, 1.21.4 music list, 1.21.5 dry foliage, 1.21.11 environment attributes + #rrggbb colours, 26.1 patch feature removed + dragon fight field, 26.2 lake rule fields).

## Item model states owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES` off. Verified vanilla facts: bow = using_item condition then use_duration (scale 0.05, thresholds 0.65/0.9), byte-for-byte equal to vanilla bow.json on 1.21.4, 1.21.11 and 26.2; crossbow uses crossbow/pull 0.58/1.0 + charge_type (1.21.11 swapped outer layers vs 1.21.4); on_shelf context exists from 1.21.9; 26.x adds an optional `transformation` field we do not emit. Gun aim = a silent never-finishing consumable whose consume event is cancelled; held items refresh every 2 ticks; plugin 'mode' is one string (strings[0]) plus separate flags. NOT verified: how items look/switch in a real client; no javac on 1.21.4/1.21.8/26.1.2; the studio tab was renamed 'In hand' -> 'In game'. 1.21.1 legacy emitter is out of scope.

## Sound Studio UI owner items (agent report 2026-10-10)
Stays off behind `cyrus_studios_enabled`; library audition off until `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED=1`. Decide: the library licence; whether committing the waveform OUTLINES (library-peaks.json, 64 levels per file, metadata not audio; not legal advice) is acceptable; sound candidates run as change builds on Saka (a new mod version each time); studio saves reach servers only on the next build; where production audio renders run (portal-to-node-2 render connection untested). Gaps vs mockup: narrower columns at 1440px (portal sidebar), header says 'mob' not 'zombie (silenced)', waveform legend below the box, cannot create a sound set from scratch in the studio. 23 sound-* screenshots in /root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/.

## Menu + quest designer owner items (2026-10-10)
Flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER` off. Caps: 8 menus, 16 quests, 6 slot rows, 10 pages, 8 actions/click, 8 steps x 3 objectives, 1-5 active quests/player, 2048 chars progress/player, one shared listener per mod. Real node-2 flights on 1.21.11 and 26.2 passed 21 RCON checks each. Not verified: any real client.

## Design v2 mockups (2026-10-10) - YOUR REVIEW NEEDED before any UI is built
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v2/: item-designer.html, menu-quest.html, mod-packs.html, import-mod.html, datapack-studio.html (+ DESIGN-NOTES.md, 28 shots/). Questions: where production item icons come from (mockups use placeholder pixel art); should settings-only edits skip the model and cost 0 tokens; is the menu/quest scope right; may a pack install with open warnings; how third-party mods are added; is the worldgen restart automatic and are dimension folders kept on uninstall; is the simulator customer-facing; approve the import attestation wording.

## Multi-game 3D research (2026-10-10)
Sonnet research pass running -> /root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/H-3d-games.md (go/no-go per game, where to start, foundation architecture).

## Foundation + community library (2026-10-10)
`feature/cyrus-r13-foundation` (worktree cyrus-r13, commit 6c91ab372b, NOT yet merged into r2): adapter asset-profile contract (Minecraft filled in, legal unreviewed), glTF sidecar manifest + legal-class ledger, worker-class job queue + content-addressed object store. 89 tests pass, tsc clean.
Owner idea 2026-10-10: every generated asset goes into a community library owned by Cyrus. DECIDED 2026-10-10: contribution is AUTOMATIC (no opt-in); ledger commit c94a65b061 (libraryEligible). Still needs before launch: ToS licence-grant wording (lawyer), content filters (trademark/real-weapon/NSFW), report/takedown. Excluded always: game-derived, third-party-licensed, imported-from-outside.

## R5 integration and delivery (`feature/cyrus-r12`, 2026-10-10)
No migration, enum or table. New OFF flags: `CYRUS_DELIVERY` (orchestrator master switch, worker), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE` (boot-test sweep, worker), `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL` (block install/publish of a version whose flight FAILED). Sound render path: worker `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=ssh` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_PORT` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN`; web `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER=relay` + `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>` + same token (ssh is refused in the web process). Rebuild the build-service image (copies `release.js`). Before `CYRUS_DELIVERY=1`: an enqueue path for the `cyrusDelivery` GAME_MOD_SYNC payload, one supervised real delivery on an owner test server, and decisions on automatic restarts + the admin cleanup of kept dimension folders. Real node-2 results: `delivery-r5-flights-2026-10-10.json`, `testflight-gate-r5-2026-10-10.json`, `sound-relay-r5-2026-10-10.json`. Docs: "Cyrus integration and delivery (R5)".

## Model Studio design + plan (2026-10-10) - YOUR REVIEW NEEDED
/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/v3-model-studio/: MODEL-STUDIO-PLAN.md (layers 1-4), 6 mockups (paint, cuboid/bone editor, car livery retexture, locked states, automatic library, AK-47 prompt flow), DESIGN-NOTES.md, 28 shots. Questions: plan placement (proposed: top "All models" plan); does "usable by anyone" in the library include "Use in project" (today's gate locks it); what happens to mods that use a removed library asset; real-weapon names (hold for review, not block); lawyer for ToS licence wording; budget for the paid AI-mesh quality test and a GPU worker; Hytale timing. Library eligibility gap closed in r2 (uploads, templates, derived content excluded). Blender headless proof of concept running -> I-blender-poc.md.
DECIDED 2026-10-10: Model Studio sits in the top "All models" plan (same tier as Texture Studio/Library). Server-side gate to follow when built.

## Host seam (2026-10-10)
`lib/cyrus/host` (settings, rate limit, audit, auth, access) merged into r2; `lib/cyrus/host/nxeon.ts` is the only bridge; `test/cyrus-host-seam.test.ts` blocks new Nxeon imports under lib/cyrus (baseline can only shrink). Decisions pending: Stripe model, SSO vs own accounts, domain, install API, DB/credentials.
## Hytale (N-hytale.md): conditional GO, adapter at maturity "planned". Blocker: each Hytale licence authenticates at most 100 servers; Nxeon would need the Game Server Provider entitlement. Official support pages 403; server/auth details from community sources.

## AI mesh / meshgen service (`feature/cyrus-r18-meshgen`, 2026-10-10)
Model Studio L4 as a flagged service: router (catalog -> template -> parts kit -> from-scratch script), cost estimate before running, node-2 sandboxed Blender worker on the job queue, checks, glb + manifest (`ai-generated-for-user`). All flags OFF, not wired into the build service, no migration. Report: `O-meshgen.md`; docs "Cyrus AI mesh (meshgen)".
1. **Pricing inputs (needed for any money figure):** set `cyrus_meshgen_price_input_per_mtok`, `..._output_per_mtok`, `..._cache_read_per_mtok` (USD per million tokens of the model you will use). Without them the UI can show tokens only. Then decide the customer price per asset: estimates are template ~5.7k tokens (measured 5.2-8k), kit ~11.6k (not measured), scratch ~19k (measured 15-20k), plus ~25 s of 4 CPU threads on node-2 per round, plus rejected rounds.
2. **Paid eval (budget decision):** 20+ real prompts per rung with a real model + vision look step, to measure success rate in <= 3 rounds and real tokens. Nothing here called a model.
3. **Isolated worker before rung 3 is ever on for customers:** the from-scratch rung runs model-written Python; the systemd sandbox held every PoC probe but a kernel escape is untested. Needs a microVM/gVisor worker (no network, no credentials). Rungs 1-2 run no model code and can use node-2 as is.
4. **GPU worker:** not needed for rungs 0-3 (Cycles CPU renders ~16-28 s). Only needed for faster previews (EEVEE) or image-to-3D (TRELLIS, MIT) later.
5. **Game budgets:** no shipped game declares `AssetProfile.meshBudget`; every real game is refused until its adapter sets one (FiveM/UE numbers need a person to check the engine docs). The flights used a made-up draft profile.
6. **Template roadmap (proposal):** next pistol/shotgun (rifle kit reuse), barrel/drum + lantern (kit already does them), furniture (table/chair/shelf), sci-fi panel/terminal, melee axe/hammer/mace (the sword excludes these words today), vehicle parts much later. Known weak: the rifle `drum` magazine reads like a wheel; the wooden crate's bands are thin.
7. Switch on order when ready: `CYRUS_MESHGEN=1` on the worker host only after the build-service wiring, the plan gate (Model Studio = "All models") and the catalog registration exist; `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH=1` only after item 3.

Metadata + tagging + retrieval layer (`lib/cyrus/library/v2`): CatalogEntry v1 (situations, quality score, per-game fit, licence tier), zero-token stage A, stage-B planner/estimator with a hard budget (no model called), stage-C review data, content filters, catalog_search/catalog_get tools. Report: `M-catalog-v2.md`; docs "Cyrus asset catalog (v2)". Measured: stage A fully describes 54.7 % of the staged CC0 catalog (models 98.7 %, sprites 41.6 %), 76.9 % of SFX names. Tagging 100k assets is ~$12 / $24 / $47 at cheap/mid/top list prices (prices are inputs; verify).
1. Migration `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-10-cyrus-catalog-v2.sql` (3 new tables, additive, NOT applied).
2. Decide licence tiers per plan (`PLAN_TIERS` in `lib/cyrus/library/v2/tools.ts`).
3. Clear the proprietary SFX library per pack (licence text per folder) before customer builds; decide on real-gun pack names (flagged today).
4. Stage-B approval: tier + token cap per run (ledger table `CyrusCatalogEnrichmentRun`); suggested first step a 500-asset cheap-tier run on sprites.
5. Extend the trademark stub list; confirm "hold for owner review" for community assets named after real guns.
6. Asset-profile catalog hints for each next game (only Minecraft has them).

## Model Studio Layer 1: viewport + paint (`feature/cyrus-r16-viewport`, 2026-10-10)
Built behind flags, NOT deployed, NOT merged into a release. Docs: "Cyrus Model Studio: viewport and paint". Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-designs/impl-shots/modelstudio-*.png`. The UI follows the v3 paint mockup, which you have NOT reviewed yet: please review the mockup and these shots together.
1. **Two settings, both off:** `cyrus_studios_enabled` (existing) AND the new `cyrus_model_studio_enabled`. Until both are on, only preview accounts see /studio/model. The new key is not in the admin settings catalog yet (add it there when you want a toggle in /admin).
2. **One new table** `CyrusModelDraft` (autosave drafts; no FKs). Needs the normal schema push at deploy, before the flag. Without it autosave answers "not available" (no 500s) and saving revisions still works.
3. **Plan gate as you decided:** paint/fill/decal/layers/drafts/save = "All models" only, server side, unknown plan = closed; view/orbit/previews/install/export never gated. Lower plans get the page in view-only.
4. **Finding to decide (guns):** the new grip_in_hand check shows today's Cyrus handgun defaults put the grip ~2/16 block from where vanilla holds tools in third person (3/16 in first person, 5/16 for the template's aiming state). Cause: the re-grip is computed under the gun's own rotation. Options: (a) re-grip to the vanilla fist (my recommendation, a small change in `lib/cyrus/textures/display.ts`, it changes shipped packs), (b) keep and verify on the real-client day. Either way: one Test Flight with a real client holding the pistol.
5. **Not built yet (next tasks):** compiling painted creature skins into the delivered BetterModel model (creature paint is saved as revisions only; item paint DOES ship, through the Texture Studio save); the production transport for the server preview renderer (it runs Chromium, so only on node-2; `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW=local` is refused in production); AI model candidates (the prompt dock is shown disabled); an entry link from the mod's Assets tab; ItemCuboidSpec 3D items (plan F3).
6. **Decisions taken here (change if you disagree):** half-transparent paint on items is snapped to solid/clear (Minecraft cutout); "Fill" defaults to the whole face (Same colour is an option); mirror reflects across the model's centre plane; layers per model max 16; a dev-only sample glTF crate appears in the model list only off production.

# Cyrus Master Plan: the ultimate game-mod creation studio (Minecraft first)

Date: 2026-10-10. Owner direction: build the ultimate mod creation studio; launch is months away; other concerns later. Sources: the four owner documents (Master Update Plan, Texture & Sound plan, Minecraft Feature Roadmap, multi-game prompt), research files E, G, A, A2, B, C, D, F, and the red-team review GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md, all in `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-research/`. Research claims are labelled VERIFIED or UNVERIFIED in those files; this plan inherits their labels and adds none of its own. Sizes are S/M/L effort.

## 1. What we are building
A real game-mod **engine**, not a prompt box. The source of truth is a typed, versioned **mod project**; the AI is the author and editor inside it; deterministic generators, validators and a real-server test harness turn the project into artifacts; studios and designers edit the same project; mods compose into Mod Packs; users can bring their own mods. Minecraft is adapter #1 on a game-agnostic core.

**Principles**
1. Engine first: every feature must be typed, validated, testable, editable and composable. A prompt wrapper is not a feature.
2. Evidence over claims: no status ("built", "tested", "supported") that did not actually run. Compile, scan, boot test and functional test are separate checks.
3. Foundation for other games: shared core behind interfaces; per-game adapters (Section 4.10).
4. Honest about limits: the router tells users what a vanilla client can and cannot do.
5. Dependencies decide order, not enthusiasm (the review found five dependency inversions in the first schedule; this plan fixes them).

## 2. Decisions already made by the owner
- Plan tiers: Free and Katara get no studios; **Saka gets Sound Studio + Sound Library; the top plan (`all`, includes Yakko) gets everything** including Texture Studio + Texture Library. Tiers are cumulative.

content.content:
Cyrus stays a part of Nxeon for at least the next few months (to build a solid foundation and gather months of real Nxeon-customer usage data), then may become its own product. So:
- **Nothing breaks and nothing changes for customers:** same sign-in, same accounts, same wallet, same billing. No separate Cyrus login now.
- **Design for the split from day one (cheap now, expensive later):** Cyrus code reaches Nxeon only through a small **host seam** (sign-in/user, plan and billing, server access for install, storage, notifications). New code must not add new direct imports of Nxeon internals; where one is unavoidable it goes behind a named adapter. Cyrus tables stay Cyrus-prefixed with opaque ids for users/servers (no new foreign keys into Nxeon tables). The build service already stands alone; the engine core, asset pipelines, Test Flight and pack hosting already live under `lib/cyrus/` and stay game- and host-agnostic.
- **Later, when separating:** Nxeon implements the host side as an API (list servers, push plugin/pack/config, restart); a standalone Cyrus gets its own sign-in, wallet and billing, own database, and a standalone export (jar and pack download). The Kodely-to-Nxeon partner API is the existing pattern.
- **Not now:** no code that exists only to prepare the split beyond the seam rule and a coupling map.

## 3. Reality check on the facts (from the research)
- Cyrus builds only 1.21.1/1.21.4/1.21.8/1.21.11 on JDK 21. Compile is plain `javac --release 21 -proc:none` against a Paper-only classpath (Gradle only builds classpath files). 4 of 6 explicitly versioned Paper servers on Nxeon already run 26.x, so version support is a top lever. 26.x needs Java 25. **Correction (checked on Paper's Fill API and Maven, 2026-10-10):** stable builds exist only for 26.1.2 (build 74) and 26.2 (build 133); 26.3 has only alpha/beta builds, so the version research was wrong that 26.3 is stable. The 26.x lane starts with **26.2**, then 26.1.2; 26.3 stays preview and unpinned until Paper ships a stable build. The registry now holds the exact pins and server-jar hashes.
- No ModSpec, project/revision store, asset manifest or import flow exist. A "project" is a chain of `ModBuild` rows. `textures/` does item textures only; `sfx.ts` is interface sounds only. The Mods installer treats resource packs as unsupported. `packFormatFor` is wrong for 26.x (returns 75; 26.1 is 76-84). Plan tiers gate models only; the single gate is `gateBuild` at `create.ts:72`, bypassed when tokens are off.
- `server.properties` holds one resource pack; Paper's `Player#addResourcePack(UUID, ...)` allows several and `setResourcePack` is deprecated.
- A vanilla client with a server-pushed pack plus datapack can show items, weapons, armor, food, display-entity mobs, glyph HUDs, GUIs, enchantments, recipes, advancements, bosses, abilities, commands, sounds, biomes and structures. Client-mod-only: brand-new block types, native entity models, free-form HUD widgets, custom keybinds, custom sky.
- Build service auth: it can run on a subscription login. Before ANY public launch, switch to an API key and re-measure cost (not blocking development now).
- Jars are not reproducible today (`jar --create` without `--date`).

## 4. Engine design
### 4.1 Mod project model + revisions (size L)
Typed project: `ModSpec`/content IR (items, mobs, abilities, GUIs, quests, recipes, loot, biomes...), code files, assets, datapacks, config, dependencies, tests, requirement IDs. Stored as immutable revisions with diffs; each revision traces to exact inputs and toolchain; the last passing revision is always preserved. `schemaVersion` with explicit migrations; JSON Schema as the portable contract, Zod types in code. New tables (project, revision, asset, namespace) need an owner-approved DB migration deploy. Chat history is not the project.

### 4.2 Registries and reserved namespaces (S-M)
Capability registry, **version registry**, **identifier registry**, asset registry with provenance. Each project reserves a namespace `nx_<hash>` at creation so IDs, keys, permissions, sound keys, glyph ranges and model paths are collision-free by construction. Version registry holds exact pack format per version (one `pack.mcmeta` style per version family), JDK, classpath hash, capability flags (item model definitions from 1.21.4; Dialog API 1.21.7+; Folia support), status (`preview/supported/deprecated/blocked`). Contract-tested against Paper's Fill API.

### 4.3 Capability router + task spec (M)
After the prompt check: classify what the request needs (plugin / plugin + resource pack / datapack / future client mod), disclose limits, show an editable plan and acceptance criteria before tokens are spent. One schema: this is the Master Plan's `CyrusTaskSpec`, the Roadmap's Mod Specification and the asset manifest. Tier gate is applied here and again inside the build service request.

### 4.4 Generators, build and reproducibility (M)
Deterministic generators emit code/data/packs for common mechanics from the IR; free-form AI code is the fallback. Build: `javac` per version lane (JDK 21 and JDK 25 side by side, per-version `--release`, classpath files fetched by checksum, exact stable pin), scan, package. Make jars byte-stable (`jar --date`, sorted inputs); record **engine release id** (prompt version + sheets + rules + scanner hash + image digest), source/classpath/output hashes, scan report and SBOM per artifact. Rename CYR-004 to "immutable javac/classpath/template".

### 4.5 Managed plugins, Pack Loader, pack hosting (M)
- **ManagedPlugin** records: pinned version per Minecraft family, installed on first dependent mod, ref-counted, not user-removable while depended on. Hosts the Pack Loader and BetterModel.
- **Nxeon Pack Loader**: sends N packs by UUID with `addResourcePack`, per-pack required/optional, accept-rate telemetry, Geyser/Floodgate detection. `server.properties` only as fallback. Conflict engine detects an existing pack owner (ResourcePackManager, Oraxen, Nexo).
- **Pack hosting**: object storage on an Nxeon domain (provider not named to customers), content-addressed immutable URLs `/p/<sha1>.zip`, size caps, retention GC; keep it off the primary node.

### 4.6 Test Flight (M, lite first)
Disposable Paper server per target version on node-2 (MEASURED 2026-10-10 with Test Flight lite: 26.x 10.4-10.8 s boot, 722-803 MB peak RSS; 1.21.11 on JDK 21 18.0 s, 878 MB; whole flight 12-20 s; see docs "Cyrus Test Flight (R0)"): boot, plugin enabled, RCON commands, `datapack list`, log matcher, clean shutdown. Later: MockBukkit logic tests, Mineflayer scenario bots (MIT, supports through 26.1), performance scenarios. Honest per-check status table; no "success" if a required stage was skipped. Concurrency capped (a past node crash came from parallel builds).

### 4.7 Asset pipeline and studios
Shared studio core + per-game profile. Minecraft = pixel profile.
- **Texture** (top plan): LLM writes a pixel spec (palette + shapes), deterministic renderer draws it (raise the 400-op / 16-64 px limits for skins and larger atlases), optional pixel-model candidates later; per-mod **Style DNA** (palette ramps, outline rule, noise) for consistency; per-version validation; AI edits arrive as non-destructive candidates.
- **Sound** (Saka+): `SoundSpec` (events -> layers -> processing); tag the 514-file library by filename category; synthesis presets; processing in the browser from WAV, **server-side ffmpeg/libvorbis to mono Ogg Vorbis**; new namespaced sound keys played by the plugin (and silence the vanilla base mob; never override vanilla keys globally); mandatory subtitle keys. A complete mob set: ambient, hurt, death, step, attack, ability, spawn.
- **Models** (26.x first): `RigSpec` compiled by Nxeon code (3 archetypes, 5 procedural clips) to .bbmodel for **BetterModel** (MIT, pinned managed plugin). Handgun and similar items use static item models with display transforms, sounds and particles, no engine. Do not embed Blockbench (GPL app); do not depend on ModelEngine/FreeMinecraftModels/CraftEngine.
- **Quality bar**: rubric + metrics (texture palette size, contrast, edge density, banding, transparent policy; sound mono, true peak, loudness band per role, silence ratio) plus a vision-model judge calibrated on 100 owner-labelled samples; owner reviews a gallery.
| 13-14 | Datapack MVP: typed emitters per version, mcdoc validation, boot + RCON check | Valid datapack loads on every listed version |
| 15-16 | Import (source-only): ingestion limits, allowlist, attestation, strict vs attested scan, revision 0, change planner | An uploaded simple plugin source is edited by prompt, rebuilt, scanned, tested, installed; history kept |
| 16 | Public pass-rate page + evidence badges (boot-tested on exact version, scan hash, SBOM) | Numbers come from real runs |

### R3 Creatures, full studios, designers (L; after R2 is stable)
- **26.x creature pipeline**: BetterModel managed plugin; RigSpec compiler; 3 archetypes; 5 clips; banshee end to end; hitboxes and attacks; performance budget per server (T).
- **Full Texture and Sound Studios**: layers/undo/palettes/selection/tiling preview/onion skin; waveform, spectrum, layering; reference-image-to-spec via a vision model; asset history with diffs.
- **Gameplay Designers**, one at a time: Custom Item Designer; ability/event graph (typed triggers -> conditions -> actions compiled to validated code, no arbitrary scripts) with a verified component library; then GUI, quests/NPCs, bosses, progression, minigames. Auto-generated Dialog config screens (1.21.7+).
- **Playtest scripts** from spec acceptance criteria (Mineflayer).

### R4 World and reach (L)
Biomes, structures, dimensions (restart rule); glyph HUDs with honest limits (avoid core shaders); "Try it" throwaway server link; multi-version build from one ModSpec; legacy `custom_model_data` emitter for 1.21.1; Server Doctor for servers with no Cyrus mods; mod health telemetry (opt-in).

### R5 Beyond Minecraft Java (own programmes)
Fabric client-mod pipeline (narrow); the other five games as adapters (multi-game prompt, per-game maturity ladder); realistic 3D/PBR asset profile; Bedrock conversion. Each starts only when the previous layers are stable.

## 6. Cross-cutting
- **Testing/eval**: extend the existing harness (28 prompts, 28/28 built, 13/13 loaded on v6) to 100+ prompts per version; golden pack snapshots (canonical JSON + sorted file list + sha1); property tests for merge laws (idempotent, order-stable, no key loss); javap-verified API sheets in CI; contract test of the version registry; mutation corpus for conflicts. Per-version pass rates published only when measured.
- **Quality bar**: Style DNA, rubric metrics, vision-judge calibration, owner gallery sign-off.
- **Pricing**: show an estimate before building; price assets by measured work; no charge if validation fails before delivery; per-feature reserve rows (reconcile `katara/saka/yakko` vs `katara/saka/all` naming); free tier gets no assets and per-device/IP caps.
- **Operations**: treat prompt + sheets + rules + scanner + image as one engine release with canary and auto-rollback on eval regression; per-feature kill switches (asset generation, import, packs); node-2 capacity budget for test servers; prompt-injection hygiene (imported text only as quoted data, no network for the model, path allow-list on diffs).

I'll define a BossAction set mirroring item actions (damage, heal, potion effects, knockback, pull, projectiles, particles, sound, messages) plus new boss-specific ones like summon, leap, dash, self-heal, and shield, with target selection modes like nearest, random, all-in-arena, or farthest, each capped by a max count. content.thinking:
I'm considering whether bosses should get their own dedicated hub, similar to Gameplay, wired into the main class, with a "boss" subcommand integrated into the existing command delegation chain where GameplayCommand falls back to DesignCommand.

For the reload flow, I'm figuring out whether BossCommand should intercept "reload" itself, delegate to the previous executor first so items/menus/quests reload and print normally, then separately trigger bosses.load() and print its own notes. I also need to handle config version migration, since bosses would need to reset `bosses.*` and `hud.*` settings on version bumps, following the same pattern Gameplay uses for tracking file version at construction time.

On the drops side, I'm thinking boss drops should be a list of entries referencing either vanilla items or design items by key (from the project's item designer), with count and chance fields, possibly also supporting a loot table reference tied to the project's datapack.

For distribution, I want a mode flag letting drops go either to a shared ground pile or individually to each contributing player above a minimum damage share, which naturally prevents loot stealing. I'm also sketching difficulty scaling so boss health and damage adjust based on how many players are in the arena.

For performance caps, I'm thinking max live bosses per mod (1-4, hard cap 4), minion caps per boss and plugin-wide, a shared attack tick timer at 10 ticks minimum, and reusing the existing Budget class for actions/entities/tasks/particles/projectiles rather than creating a separate boss-specific budget — though the projectile cap of 3 per attack feels a bit restrictive for boss fights.

Now I'm defining arena rules: a spawn-centered sphere/cylinder with radius 8-64 determines who counts as "in the fight," with leashing to pull the boss back if it strays and despawn/cleanup after an empty timeout (10-600s). I'm also adding griefing protections like no block damage, bossbar visibility limited to arena players, and an enrage timer (60-3600s) for max fight duration.

Spawning options: an op-only command with coordinates, or a consumable summon item with no other abilities to avoid conflicts, capped by maxAlive limits per boss id and per mod. Cleanup logic handles death (drops, minion removal, bossbar teardown) and server shutdown/plugin disable scenarios.

For stray entities, I'm marking bosses and minions as non-persistent so they vanish naturally on chunk unload rather than saving incorrectly, plus a periodic validity check to catch and clean up any that go invalid without dying properly, and a startup sweep to remove leftover tagged entities from crashes. Now I'm working out the boss bar presentation using Adventure's BossBar API for title, color, and overlay style.

I'm now designing the phase system itself—each boss has a sequence of phases tied to decreasing health thresholds, with each phase defining its own attack pool, attack timing, entrance effects (messages, sounds, particles, summons), and optional self-buffs, ensuring phases only progress forward. I'm also structuring individual attacks with telegraph warnings, cooldowns, range checks, and target selection logic (nearest, random, farthest, etc.) before getting into the actual attack actions.

For boss actions, I'm covering damage, knockback, pull-toward-boss, potion effects, and projectile launches, working through how to give normally-harmless projectiles like snowballs real damage by tagging them and applying custom hit damage through a listener.

I'm also planning compositional pieces: particle effects, sounds, messages to targets, leap and slam moves that reuse the generic targeting/damage/knockback system (so slam is really just an attack with radius-based targeting), and summon actions for spawning entities.

I'm also thinking through budget constraints per attack—caps on action counts, target limits, projectiles, tasks, and summons—plus restricting boss base entities to a vanilla allowlist like zombies, husks, and skeletons.

I'm going through the rest of the vanilla mob allowlist, weighing which bosses are too disruptive to allow as bases—excluding ones that explode, split, teleport away, or fly, like creepers, slimes, endermen, ghasts, and phantoms—while keeping sturdier melee-type mobs as viable options.

For stats, I'm settling on a max health cap, noting that vanilla's attribute cap is 1024 but Spigot/Paper defaults allow up to 2048, so I'm leaning toward a safer 1024 ceiling.

I'm mapping out other attribute ranges: armor 0-30, attack damage 0-40, movement speed 0.1-0.5, knockback resistance 0-1, and follow range 16-64, cross-referencing their Bukkit attribute names for compatibility.

Compat only has ATTACK_DAMAGE, ATTACK_SPEED, and MAX_HEALTH mapped, so I need generic-prefix fallbacks for the rest on 1.21.1. Since I can't touch Compat without breaking item golden hashes, I'll create a separate boss-specific compat file rendered per version, keeping item outputs untouched.

Now I'm thinking through the boss's name handling (styled text, name visibility) and equipment slots like main hand and helmet.

Equipment can use either vanilla items or design items for display purposes only, since abilities don't fire for mobs wielding them, and drop chance should always be zero so bosses can't be farmed for gear. For immunities, I'm handling fire, fall, projectile, drowning, and explosion by canceling damage events based on cause, which keeps things arena-friendly.

I'm also sketching out an EncounterDesign concept — an arena event with waves of mobs and/or bosses, triggered by command, item, or quest, with wave definitions specifying entities, counts, and advancement conditions.

For the arena itself, I'm thinking of a fixed location or "here" at the summoner, with radius-based rules rather than physical walls — players who leave simply drop out. Each wave spawns vanilla mobs or boss entities from an allowlist, using ring or random spawn patterns, and advances either when cleared or after a timer. Completion grants rewards to participants via the same Drop component, while failure (all dead, players leaving, or timeout) triggers cleanup. I'm capping alive mobs per encounter at 24 and limiting active encounters to 2 per mod to keep things performant.

I should check whether this integrates with the quest system — a "kill boss X" objective could reuse vanilla kill_entity objectives, though I may just note that as a future addition rather than building it now. Bosses spawned during encounter waves will reuse the existing boss runtime, and for the simulator I want a deterministic tick-based fight sim driven by scripted damage, phase thresholds, attack selection using the same seeded Java Random port, boss bar progress, health scaling, drop rolls, and cap/despawn enforcement — I should look at simulate.ts to reuse that JavaRandom implementation. For configurability, boss and encounter parameters go under their own namespaced config keys with clamping via DesignConfig, and migrations should reset those namespaces whenever the config version bumps.

Next I'll check gameplay/params.ts for how edits get applied, then wire up the service layer. After that, I plan real test flights on node-2 against Paper 1.21.11 and 26.2, using RCON to list/spawn bosses, verify entity existence, damage the boss via the `/damage` command to trigger phase transitions, kill it to test drop behavior and minion cleanup, and verify despawn timing when no players are present in the arena — though I note vanilla `/bossbar list` won't show Adventure-based client-side boss bars, so I'll need another way to verify those.

Since Test Flight has no real players, I realize many combat behaviors (targeted attacks, aggro) can't be exercised normally since the boss AI needs living targets. I'm thinking a debug command like `boss cast <id> <attack>` that targets a tagged dummy mob would let me trigger attacks manually and verify damage via RCON by checking the dummy's health data — a solid way to validate attack execution without real players.

Now I want to check the earlier real-flight harness test file to see how they set up RCON for Test Flight runs.

content.thinking:
I'm thinking about the cleanest way to extend validateGameplay and compileMod to handle boss/encounter kinds, considering whether to add a separate validator in boss/spec.ts, but I need to watch out for circular imports between boss/spec and gameplay/spec.

To sidestep the cycle, boss/spec should only depend on the base item spec and expose its own helpers, with gameplay/spec importing `validateBossKinds` from it rather than the reverse. I also realize designKind and validateGameplay need direct changes anyway, since designKind currently returns null for unknown kinds like "boss", "encounter", or "hud", so I'll extend it to recognize those too.

I'm now weighing whether boss validation needs access to the items map for drop references, which means passing an explicit `items: Map<string, ItemDesign>` parameter rather than importing gameplay/spec directly — keeping the dependency direction clean as gameplay/spec → boss/spec → base spec. I still need to figure out whether HUD requires its own distinct design kind or can reuse an existing pattern.

I'm sketching out a HudDesign kind with glyph-based bars and text elements (health, quest progress, custom counters), layout definitions per delivery channel (action bar, boss bar, scoreboard), and a bitmap font provider mapping textures to private-use codepoints from the project's glyph block — the pack builder would need to emit the font JSON and textures, so I'll check the identifier glyph block allocation and pack builder logic later.

For compiling, I'm thinking through how compileMod should branch: if boss/encounter/HUD designs exist, pull in the boss library and classes, reusing the gameplay path and wiring bosses into the main gameplay class. I want to avoid changing existing gameplay golden hashes, so the gameplay hub should only expand when bosses are actually present, even though that means the hub still gets included somewhat unnecessarily if bosses exist without menus or quests.

I'm weighing whether this is too bloated — a boss-only mod shouldn't really need menu/quest scaffolding — against the lower-risk option of just reusing the existing gameplay machinery as-is. A cleaner approach would introduce a needGameplay flag based on whether menus or quests exist, skipping gameplay components and construction entirely when not needed, with the boss hub wrapping whichever executor is present instead.

Before writing the actual code, I want to check the remaining wiring files — prompts.js, server.js, the asset request/sync modules, and the cyrus-mods doc/meta/create/types files — to see how they changed in the relevant commit.

content.thinking:
I'm sketching out a HUD design schema alongside the existing design folder structure, defining glyphs as pixel art with configurable font height and ascent, plus bar elements that reference a data source and render using segmented styles with full/half/empty glyph states.

For glyph art, I'm deciding against reusing texture specs since those generate unwanted item models — instead I'll use self-contained inline pixel grids with a small palette, written via the existing PNG encoder in lib/cyrus, and I'll bundle built-in presets like hearts, mana drops, bar segments, and other common icons so the model can reference them by name and color rather than drawing pixels from scratch.

content.thinking:
Since it compiles in TypeScript, I'll now write the actual runner, modeling it on cyrus-gameplay-real.ts, starting with a javac-only version before expanding to the full Java test flow with lanes, builds, scans, and RCON flight checks. I'll leave the expected RCON strings as placeholders for now until I can see the real outputs.

For the ember_warden flight on 1.21.11, I'm working through the sequence of checks: confirming the plugin loads, verifying the `bosstrials` summary output, checking the boss list description matches the expected format (entity type, health, phases, attacks, arena size, bar style, spawn method, minions), and confirming the encounter list output for ash_trial matches the expected waves/sizes/rewards format.

Then I'm walking through spawning ember_warden via command and checking the resulting entity count, health, phase, and boss status output including bar text, participants, and enraged state. For the damage test, I'm working out the armor mitigation math for a generic damage type against 6 armor and toughness, since the formula drives the expected health after a 150-damage hit.

Taking that mitigated damage down to about 157.2 health drops the fraction below 0.6, triggering phase 2 with the "Ashen Fury" bar and a resistance buff; a second 150-damage hit, further reduced by the 20% resistance, pushes health down into phase 3 territory around 43 remaining. I decide to avoid asserting exact health numbers and instead check for the "phase 3/3 p3" substring, while also considering whether invulnerability frames after the first hit would block the second damage command from landing.

For spawning the test dummy, I'm using a command to summon a villager with no AI near the boss entity, tagged for tracking. I'm second-guessing whether vanilla mob AI could cause problems -- wither skeletons won't target villagers, but a zombie-type boss might, so I should stick with the ember warden type for this test case.

Then testing the slam ability cast against the dummy: at close range it should deal roughly 4.5 damage after difficulty scaling, bringing the villager from 20 to 15.5 health, and I'm confirming that mob-sourced damage isn't affected by difficulty multipliers the way player damage is, so the expected health reading checks out.

I need to verify the server's actual difficulty setting via the `difficulty` command since Test Flight might override Paper's default, then feed that into the TypeScript twin calculation. After that I'm checking the cinders ability summons two blazes correctly, confirming the minion count via entity selectors, verifying boss status reports two minions, and then moving into leash behavior testing for the boss entity.

For the leash distance test, I'm wary of teleporting the boss 40 blocks away since that might push it outside the ticking spawn chunk radius (around 2 chunks, roughly 32 blocks in 1.21), risking the entity becoming unloaded or invalid before I can check leash status — so I should use a safer distance like 30 blocks to stay within loaded chunks while still testing the leash range.

Next I need to verify killing the boss with no valid participants correctly results in it being defeated with zero drops going to nobody, that its minions get removed afterward (confirmed by the minion tag query failing), and that the status command properly reports "No bosses alive" along with the last defeat summary showing zero drop stacks and the two minions removed.

Then I'll check ground-drop behavior by spawning grave_lord and killing it, expecting drops to scatter on the ground including a diamond item and XP orbs. After that I'll test empty-despawn by setting a short despawn timer, waiting past it, and confirming the boss despawns due to no players being nearby, then move to testing the ash_trial encounter start and verifying the wave-1 entity count.

Clearing wave 1 should trigger wave 2 after a short delay, with a different mob count to verify; the encounter's empty-seconds timer shouldn't trigger a fail during this window. For wave 2 I need to account for a fixed timer duration before it auto-advances to wave 3, regardless of whether the mobs are killed early, and then confirm the boss spawns for the final wave after its own delay.

Killing the final boss should complete the encounter and grant the reward. Next I'm checking config validation: clamping an out-of-range health value and an invalid phase threshold, verifying the migration system bumps old configs to the current version, confirming the params command reports correct stats, and checking the logs for clean plugin disable behavior with no errors — bringing the total to over 20 RCON checks.

Then I'll edit the health and slam damage values in the config, repackage with the old jar, and confirm params reflects the new numbers. For the TypeScript twin of the boss check command, I need to build a simulate.ts that mirrors Java's Random behavior (nextDouble, nextInt, shuffle) and replicates the check() logic with proper defaults — being careful that Java's %.2f formatting uses HALF_UP rounding while JS's toFixed relies on binary rounding, which could cause mismatches on edge-case values.

I'm working through the scaled health and damage math for various difficulty tiers and player counts, confirming the formatted outputs match. Now I'm mapping out the drop and pick simulations using seeded Random instances, and replicating Java's exact shuffle algorithm for list randomization.

I'm checking Java's legacy nextInt(bound) algorithm to make sure the bias-correction logic is faithfully replicated, since java.util.Random's behavior is version-stable even in Java 17+. Next I need to work out the fight-phase simulation logic.

For the bare command case, BossCommand should print the design items summary followed by our own boss/encounter summary line.

For the damage command, I'm checking that "Applied 150.0 damage to..." formats correctly, and that the villager's health reads back as expected via `data get entity`. I'm also considering whether a NoAI villager actually responds to knockback velocity from the slam attack, since NoAI mobs may ignore physics-based pushes, though it likely won't affect the outcome.

I'm also worried about whether the summoned villager stays within the 6-block range of the boss by the time the cast triggers, since the wither skeleton's AI could cause it to wander slightly, though a second of movement shouldn't push it out of range. More importantly, the target-selection logic grabs all nearby LivingEntities (excluding players, armor stands, and self) within a bounding box, sorts by distance, and caps at six -- so naturally-spawned mobs like chickens or sheep near the test area could also get caught in the hit, which might break an assertion expecting exactly "on 1 target" if the dummy isn't the sole nearest entity.

Given that risk, I think it's safer to loosen the expected test string to just match the "Cast slam of ember_warden#1 on" prefix and "(test targets" fragment rather than an exact target count, while keeping the dummy's health check exact since it'll be hit regardless as long as it's within the six-target cap.

For the `cast-cinders` ability, since the caster targets only itself and the targets list ends up empty, I expect the message to read "on 0 targets" (using the plural form since count isn't 1), and the cast should otherwise succeed fine. For minion counts, three summon casts with a max-alive cap of 4 should net out to 2 + 2 + 0 = 4 total, respecting the budget check that blocks summoning once minions.size() reaches 4. After the boss is defeated, I expect the "minions removed" count to report 4 as well, since the removal logic should tally all valid minions cleared from the fight.

For the final boss death scenario triggered by `/kill`, I'm working out that the EntityDeathEvent handler clears drops, checks participant damage, and since there was no damage tracked at all, the qualifying list is empty, producing "nobody (no participant did 10% of the damage)" in the output. I should check if the test setup sets spawnChunkRadius to 0, or try using forceload to manually keep that area loaded.

Since console commands resolve relative coordinates against the world spawn position, I can use forceload with a tilde-based area to force-load a region around spawn—something like a 48x48 block zone covering roughly 20 chunks to ensure that spot stays active.

Force-loaded chunks also receive ticket level 31, meaning they're fully entity-ticking, which confirms the isChunkLoaded check will work correctly once I add this forceload step after the difficulty check.

content.content:
## Cyrus menu and quest designers (R3)

Branch `feature/cyrus-r11` (from `feature/cyrus-r2`, 2026-10-10). MASTER-PLAN R3 "Designers" (quest / NPC and GUI designer ideas) and RESEARCH-PLAN "Fourth document" 3.3 (Quest and NPC Designer) and 3.5 (GUI Designer). Extends "Cyrus gameplay designers (R3)" (same philosophy: typed IR, hard caps, verified Java components, deterministic codegen, every value a config.yml setting, no arbitrary code). **Nothing is deployed or switched on**: it ships under the existing OFF flag `CYRUS_DESIGNER`; off, nothing is decided and every request is byte-identical. **Not plan-gated** (assets referenced by a design keep their own gates; installing/keeping never gated). Host seam: no new Nxeon imports, no new tables (designs stay `CyrusProjectAsset` rows of kind `design`), no new asset kind.

### 1. Design files and the kind discriminator
Still one file per design at `assets/designs/<id>.json` (the existing `design` asset kind; the router, prompt, validator bundle, sync and Dockerfile entries are the designer's, extended). A top-level `kind` says what a file is: absent or `"item"` = ItemDesign (unchanged; `ItemDesignSchema` only gained the optional literal `kind: "item"`, so every existing item file validates and compiles byte for byte: the R3 golden hashes still match, tested), `"menu"` = MenuDesign, `"quest"` = QuestDesign. Items, menus and quests share one id space. A mod may have only menus/quests.

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/spec.ts` | the IR (Zod): `MenuDesignSchema` (chest / dialogue), `QuestDesignSchema`, `GAMEPLAY_CAPS`, `GAMEPLAY_LIMITS`, `designKind`, `validateMenu` / `validateQuest`, `validateGameplay` (the whole mod: items through the unchanged item validator + cross-file checks), `arbitrageLoops`, `progressEntryChars` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay.v1.schema.json` | the portable MenuDesign / QuestDesign contract (generated) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/java.ts`, `gameplay/components.ts` | the verified gameplay components (Java + metadata), `gameplayLibraryHash()` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/compile.ts` | `compileMod(inputs, ctx)`: item-only mods go to the unchanged `compileDesigns`; otherwise items + menus + quests + main class + plugin.yml + config.yml; `menuParams` / `questParams` / `modParams` |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/params.ts` | `applyGameplayEdits`, `recompileModWithEdits` (edit without regenerating) |
| `lib/cyrus/designer/gameplay/simulate.ts` | the TS twin: `GameplaySimulator`, `Pagination`, `encodeProgress` / `decodeProgress`, `progressSample` |
| `scripts/cyrus/gameplay-golden.ts` | golden record (`test/fixtures/cyrus-gameplay/golden.json`), `--print <file>` review aid |
| `test/cyrus-gameplay.test.ts`, `test/cyrus-gameplay-real.ts`, `test/fixtures/cyrus-gameplay/` | pure suite, node-2 runner, the showcase mod (2 items, 2 menus, 4 quests) |
| `services/modbuilder/designer-gameplay-example.json` | the prompt example (dialogue + quest + config-list shop) |

Changed: `lib/cyrus/designer/{spec,compile,route,sync,service-entry}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/assets/{request,sync}.ts`, `lib/cyrus/meta.ts`, `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts`, `lib/modbuilder/{create,types}.ts`, `services/modbuilder/{server,prompts,designs,textures}.js` + `designer-spec.js` (regenerated) + `Dockerfile`, `scripts/cyrus/build-designer-artifacts.ts`, `test/modbuilder-pipeline.test.ts`.

### 2. MenuDesign
- **Chest**: `{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "menu", style: "chest", id, title (32), rows 1-6, filler?, buttons?: [{ slot, icon, actions?, cost?, permission?, hideWithoutPermission? }], list?: { slots, prev: {slot, icon}, next: {slot, icon}, source }, permission?, permissions?, openWith? }`. `source` is typed, never code: `{ type: "fixed", entries: [clickables ≤ 54] }` or `{ type: "config", currency: item | xp_levels | economy | free, entries: [{ material, amount 1-64, price, name? }] }` (a shop the OWNER edits in config.yml `lists.<menu id>`; never reset by an update).
- **Dialogue**: `{ style: "dialogue", speaker, speakerIcon?, lines 1-6 (80 chars), choices 1-5 }`, laid out by DialogueMenu (speaker slot 4, lines on a book slot 13, choices centred in the bottom row). Inventory based on every version: Paper's Dialog API (registry capability `dialogApi`, 1.21.7+, experimental) is not used.
- **Icon**: exactly one of `material` (any vanilla item; display only) or `item` (a design item, shown as a copy WITHOUT its identity), optional `model` (own namespace, 1.21.4+), name, lore (6), amount, glint.
- **Click actions (≤ 8, closed set)**: `open_menu`, `close`, `back` (stack of 8), `next_page`, `prev_page`, `give_item` (vanilla or design item, ≤ 4 per click), `send_message`, `actionbar`, `play_sound`, `potion_effect`, `heal` (all on the clicking player; the subset of the ability graph), `run_ability` (an item ability of this mod), `start_quest`, `abandon_quest`, `choose_branch`, `open_quest_log`. No command, no other player.
- **Costs**: items (vanilla material WITHOUT a design identity, or a design item BY identity; menu icons never count), XP levels, or money through the allowlisted Vault API 1.7 (`lib/cyrus/import/deps.json` `vault-api`, compile-only, never shaded; plugin.yml `softdepend: [Vault]`; the bridge class is created only when the Vault plugin is installed; without Vault + an economy the click is refused with "This server has no economy (Vault) set up…"). Only mods with money costs get `VaultMoney.java` and the dep (`compileMod().deps`), which the build service puts on the javac classpath.
- **Opening**: `/<mod> menu <id> [player]` (unless `openWith.command: false`), right-click with a design item (`openWith.item`; that item may not have right-click abilities), or an NPC: right-clicking an entity tagged `<ns>.npc.<menu id>` (vanilla `/tag`; the interaction is cancelled so a villager's trade screen does not open). Quest NPCs = dialogue menus with `npc: true`.

### 3. QuestDesign
`{ schemaVersion: 1, kind: "quest", id, title (40), description?, icon?, requires?: [quest ids] (≤ 4, a chain), start?: "command" | "menu", repeat?: { mode: once | repeatable | daily | weekly, cooldownSeconds? }, steps: [1-8 { id, text, objectives: [1-3] }], branches?: { prompt?, options: [2-3 { id, label, icon?, steps 1-4, rewards? }] }, rewards?: [≤ 8], failure?: { onDeath?: keep | reset_step | fail, timeLimitSeconds?, abandon? }, progressBar?, permission?, permissions? }`.
- **Objectives (closed set)**: `kill_entity` (vanilla type and/or kinds), `collect_item` (`inventory` = have it, checked on pickup / inventory close / the 1 s timer, or `pickup` = count pickups; `take` hands the items in when the step completes, all or nothing), `craft_item` (shift-click counts min(matrix stacks) x result), `visit_location` (world, x, y, z, radius), `break_block` (blocks placed by a player are not counted: 4096 remembered, not across restarts), `talk` (opening a dialogue menu of this mod by any route), `survive` (seconds alive and online while the step is active; death restarts the count).
- **Branching**: after the main steps a quest with branches waits in state "choose": a choice menu opens one tick later (`/<mod> quests choose <id>` reopens it), or a dialogue's `choose_branch` picks; then the branch steps follow; rewards = quest + chosen branch.
- **Repeat**: daily / weekly = a ROLLING cooldown of 24 h / 7 days after the last completion (not a calendar reset; no timezone); `repeatable` default 0 s; every cooldown is a setting.
- **Rewards (closed set)**: `give_item` (overflow drops at the feet), `xp` (points or levels), `potion_effect`, `advancement` (only `<ns>:<path>` of THIS project's data pack; the service checks the workspace's `assets/datapack` specs; a missing one at runtime logs once and grants nothing), `run_ability`, `send_message`.
- **Commands**: `/<mod> quests` (players: their quests and states; console: definitions), `quests log` (GUI), `quests start|abandon|info|choose <id>`, `quests list`, `quests check` (ops), `quests reset <player>` (`<ns>.quests.admin`). Progress on the actionbar when it changes (unless `progressBar: false`).
- **Progress persistence (QuestStore)**: the player's PersistentDataContainer `<ns>:quests` (saved with the player file, no database), versioned text `q1|<quest>,<A|C|D>,<step id>,<branch id>,<c0>.<c1>.<c2>,<started>,<completions>,<last>|…` sorted by quest id, at most 2048 characters per player per mod (the validator proves the worst case fits: `progress_oversize`). Migration-safe against the CURRENT definitions: unknown format -> copied to `<ns>:quests_backup` and reset; removed quests dropped; a step or branch that no longer exists restarts that quest (completions kept); counts clamped to the current targets. The TS codec is identical (checked on the real JVM, below).

### 4. Caps and limits
`GAMEPLAY_CAPS` (inclusive; schema refuses outside, runtime config loader clamps to the same): rows 1-6; slot 0-53; icon amount 1-64; item cost 1-2304; XP level cost 1-1000; money 0.01-1,000,000; give 1-64; heal 0-20; potion 1-1200 ticks, amplifier 0-4; volume 0-2, pitch 0.5-2; kill 1-1000; collect 1-2304; craft 1-1000; break 1-10000; survive 10-7200 s; visit radius 1-64; x/z ±30,000,000, y ±2048; repeat cooldown 0-2,592,000 s; time limit 60-604,800 s; XP points 1-100,000, levels 1-100; config-list amount 1-64; `general.menu_click_cooldown_ticks` 2-40 (runtime). `GAMEPLAY_LIMITS`: 8 menus, 16 quests, 30 design files per mod (6 items as before), 54 buttons, 45 list slots, 54 fixed entries, 270 config entries, 10 pages, 8 actions per click, 5 choices, 6 lines, 8 steps, 3 objectives per step, 3 branches of ≤ 4 steps, 8 rewards, 4 prerequisites, back stack 8, active quests per player `general.max_active_quests` 1-5 (default 3; so ≤ 15 tracked objectives per player), 2048 progress characters. Listeners: ONE ObjectiveTracker (9 handlers, one per event kind) + one shared 1 s timer per mod, never one per quest.

I'll draft a shorter version of the boss documentation for after flights, then shift to sketching out the HUD design schema, defining glyphs with presets, colors, and keys.

Now I'm fleshing out the bars, channels (actionbar, bossbar, sidebar), and parts structure for the HUD, along with value sources like health, food, and xp level.

I'm trimming scope here—dropping quest_progress since it needs the full quest fraction API which isn't built yet, and sticking to the honest, implementable sources: health, food, xp_level, armor, air, ability_charges, ability_cooldown, and boss_health, each producing a value/max pair.

For delivery, I'm thinking through actionbar updates (capped tick rate since vanilla fades after 60 ticks and overlaps with other actionbar writers), a per-player Adventure boss bar tied to the show condition, and a per-player scoreboard sidebar using a dummy objective.

For the sidebar lines, I'm using unique internal entry strings ("l0" through "l7") paired with Paper's customName component for display text and numbered scores for ordering, falling back gracefully if customName isn't available on older versions.

On conflicts, replacing the player's scoreboard breaks other plugins (TAB, team colors), so I need to guard this by only taking over if the player's current scoreboard is the main one or already ours, and restoring the main scoreboard on hide.

For the HUD font, I'm defining a font JSON with bitmap providers mapping glyph characters to PNG files plus ascent/height values, and space providers with negative advances for each distinct pixel width needed.

For codepoint allocation, I'm computing a starting block per namespace and assigning sequential codepoints to glyphs then spaces, capping things so total usage stays under 256 per block even with multiple HUD designs, and handling codepoints beyond the BMP using Java surrogate pair strings and escaped UTF-16 literals in the JSON chars array.

I think modern Minecraft (1.16+/1.20+) handles supplementary plane codepoints in bitmap font providers via codepoint-based parsing, though ItemsAdder and Oraxen both stick to BMP PUA at E000 — I should flag my supplementary-plane claim as unverified without client testing. I also need to note the bitmap PNG constraints: width must divide evenly by characters per row, and glyph cell height comes from PNG height divided by row count.

Ascent must be less than or equal to height or vanilla throws an error, and the validator needs to enforce that, though negative ascent is fine since it just shifts the glyph down. For pack integration, I'm leaning toward adding a HudFont type with glyphs and space-advance mappings that buildPack accepts directly, checking that a pack has at least one texture, sound, or font to be valid, and handling resource pack format detection based on version.

Now I need to trace sync.ts to see whether buildPack runs before or after HUD designs are checked, since HUD-only mods still need a pack generated even without textures or sounds — I should inspect the actual ordering in the file. On the Java side I'm thinking through the components: a HudDef class generated per HUD with its parts structure and value sources, a central Huds hub managing timers and per-player state, and commands for listing and managing HUDs, possibly reusing the BossCommand pattern.

I'm also considering a generic HudCommand wrapper similar to BossCommand for mods with HUDs but no bosses, constructed in the main class after the designer and bosses are set up. The tricky part is that Huds needs an optional reference to Bosses for boss_health sources, but if a HUD mod has no Bosses class in its tree, direct references would break compilation — so I'm leaning toward defining a HudValues provider interface to decouple the dependency.

Rather than hard-wiring Bosses into Huds, I'm planning to generate the lookup per-mod: each HUD definition gets its own generated subclass with a switch statement selecting health, charges, or boss lookups depending on which sources exist, so the boss reference only appears in generated code for mods that actually have bosses.

I'll add a static helper inside the boss library itself, `Bosses.hudValue(Player p, String id)`, returning the health/max array, which keeps HudSources generic and avoids a direct dependency — this does mean regenerating the boss library goldens and rerunning boss flights, but that's fine since I need to anyway.

For ability charges, I'm checking whether the designer package can access Ability's protected maxCharges field directly (yes, protected allows same-package access) and confirming how cooldown remaining time is exposed through Ability's public methods.

For HUD value computation: health fraction uses current/max health, food uses food level over 20, xp level uses getLevel, and armor isn't available since Compat only exposes attack damage, attack speed, and max health attributes -- so I'll use remaining air over maximum air instead.

For bar rendering, I need to compute full segments as floor(fraction*N), a half segment if the remainder hits 0.5 and a half glyph exists, and the rest empty, with text values formatted as rounded integers, percentages, or "value/max" fractions. Building the Adventure component requires using the custom hud font for glyph strings while keeping normal text in the default font, and I need to color glyph text white since bitmap glyph colors get tinted by the text color in Minecraft -- white preserves the original PNG colors.

I'm noting that actionbar text has a drop shadow, and glyphs inherit that shadow too; disabling it requires a shadow_color component that only exists in Adventure 4.18+ for 1.21.4+, so I'll skip that compatibility concern for now.

For the preview command, I'm designing output for `hud preview <id> <channel> <fraction>` that prints a plain-text serialization with codepoints shown as U+XXXXX tokens, a human-readable render string describing each glyph and value segment so the TS twin implementation can be verified against the same string, and a JSON serialization via GsonComponentSerializer to confirm font assignment is correct.

I also want to verify that the Gson output correctly includes the font namespace and handle potential issues with non-ASCII character escaping over RCON, and I'm sketching out `hud check` to print glyph counts, codepoint ranges, and channel info matching the TS twin. For flight tests, I'm planning coverage of hud list, hud check, preview at various fractions for actionbar/bossbar/sidebar, console-only toggle behavior, and update-tick clamping.

Reload clamping and offline pack validation should be covered too, but testing an actual client-connected resource pack sync isn't feasible here, so I'll skip that part. Now I need to look at sync.ts and check the suite results before building the pack with fonts.
